chapter_title: The Interpretation [of] the S[i]lence, the Fast, [
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶2:** [GAP-1] The one who gathers and reunites scattered goods into [GAP-2] [GAP-3] is the sustaining column of Divine Wisdom [GAP-4] because [GAP-5] [GAP-6] upward toward the [GAP-7] —

That is: the gathering function here is the divine operation by which dispersed elements of good and truth, separated through the assault of falsity, are recollected and elevated. The Pillar of Glory corresponds to the immovable structure of divine wisdom through which all purified goods ascend back to their origin — the great axis of influx connecting lower states to the celestial kingdom.

**¶3:** The Divine Humanity in its first proceeding, who dwells within the containing vessel of living divine truths, [GAP-8] wisdom [GAP-9] he is [GAP-10: called] that which they have [GAP-11] radiant with divine good [GAP-12] —

Here the First Man is the Lord's own life as it first descends into engagement with the hells — the primordial putting-on of spiritual combat. The *ship of living waters* is the doctrinal vessel formed from truths that proceed from the Divine itself, truths that are *living* because they carry within them the good of love. He dwells there: the Divine Humanity is present interiorly within these flowing truths as their animating soul.

**¶4:** [GAP-13] the whole of the spiritual world, as all regenerating goods and truths shall [GAP-14] within the eternal celestial state [GAP-15] are disseminated throughout every province of the Grand Human, it is [GAP-16] firmly established within the [GAP-17] and the interior lives of those being regenerated [GAP-18] —

This passage describes the universal scope of the Lord's operation: goods and truths that were scattered through all levels of the spiritual world are gathered, and the eternal order — the *great aeon* — is the heavenly kingdom into which they are received. The souls are the interior willing-and-understanding of those in whom regeneration proceeds, and their establishment means that the divine order is being inscribed into the very form of their life.

---
*Note:* The extensive lacunae make continuous spiritual reading difficult. The structural pattern is clear — a cosmological account of gathering, containment, and restoration — which corresponds throughout to the Lord's work of redemption: collecting dispersed goods through the column of divine wisdom, dwelling within living truth as the Divine Humanity, and establishing heavenly order across the whole Grand Human.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: [Now] the gatherer in [the worlds, who purifies and draws up the light] [he] is the Pill[a]r of Gl[or]y [the Perfect Man] because [he carries] [the light] up to the [land of light]
the [Fi]rst [M]an who dwel[ls i]n the ship of living waters [who is the] light [of the Father] he is c[alled the living one] that they have [received the] glorious [light]
[in the whole] universe as they shall [come to rest] in the great aeon [and all that] are spread in the universe, it is [firmly] established in the [aeons of light] and the so[u]ls [are gathered]

fills.explanation: Standard Kephalaia paragraph opener introducing a new identification; "Now" is the most common transitional word in expository Kephalaia paragraphs.

fills.fill: the worlds, who purifies and draws up the light
fills.explanation: The Pillar of Glory gathers in the mixed worlds (the cosmos where light is scattered); "purifies and draws up the light" is the Pillar's specific cosmological function — purifying trapped light and channeling it upward — which the spiritual reading renders as "reuniting scattered goods."
A pronoun is needed as the subject of "is the Pillar of Glory"; the Kephalaia regularly uses resumptive "he" before identification clauses.

The Perfect Man is the standard alternate epithet for the Pillar of Glory in the Kephalaia and Manichaean cosmology; the spiritual reading's "sustaining" points to this title of completed divine form.
The Pillar of Glory's essential function is to carry purified light upward; the spiritual reading confirms an ascending operation ("upward toward") requiring an active verb of conveyance.
The object carried upward by the Pillar of Glory is the purified light (= scattered divine good/truth in Swedenborg); "the light" is the standard Manichaean term for what is gathered and elevated.

The destination "up to the [X]" in Manichaean cosmology is the Land of Light (the Father's realm); corresponds to the celestial kingdom in Swedenborg, the ultimate origin to which purified goods return.
Introduces a relative clause identifying the First Man as "the light" (= wisdom in the spiritual reading); Kephalaia regularly uses relative clauses to append attributes to cosmic beings.

Completes "the light of the Father" — the First Man proceeds from the Father of Greatness, and in Swedenborg, wisdom proceeds from the Divine Love (the Father); this is a standard Manichaean attribution.
Completes "called the living one" — the First Man is called "the Living One" in Manichaean tradition, corresponding to the Divine Humanity as the source of all life in Swedenborg.

The spiritual reading indicates the subjects obtained divine good; "received the" naturally precedes "glorious [light]" and describes reception of the radiant divine good from the First Man's operation.

Completes "glorious light" — the divine good received is rendered as "light" in Manichaean natural-plane vocabulary; the spiritual reading's "radiant with divine good" corresponds to the glorious light of the Father.
The spiritual reading says "the whole of the spiritual world"; "in the whole" before "universe" establishes the universal scope of the divine operation described in this paragraph.

The spiritual reading indicates entry into the eternal celestial state; "come to rest" is the standard Manichaean expression for purified light reaching its final abode in the great aeon (= heavenly kingdom).
Bridges from the great aeon clause to the description of what is spread; "and all that are spread in the universe" introduces the scattered elements that are being gathered and established.
The spiritual reading explicitly says "firmly established"; "firmly" conveys the permanence and security of divine order being inscribed into the heavenly structure.
The standard Manichaean designation for the eternal heavenly realms where divine order is established; corresponds to the celestial kingdom's permanent provinces in Swedenborg.

The chapter's central theme is gathering; the souls (interior willing-and-understanding) are gathered into divine order, completing the threefold operation of gathering, establishing, and restoring described throughout the chapter.
